framing: From model scores to a chosen token
paragraphs: Ask a model for the next word and every token gets a probability. Another operation chooses the token. That separation explains why the same prompt can produce different answers, why testing is difficult, and what training optimizes.
A handful of ideas carries us through: turning raw scores into probabilities, working in logarithms, and measuring how costly a wrong prediction is. These ideas return throughout the book.
Follow one prompt through softmax to a sampled token. Then compare models with cross-entropy, see why confident mistakes cost so much, and estimate uncertainty in a measured pass rate.
A two-point win on fifty cases can tempt you to ship a worse model. By the end, you can examine that difference and estimate how many cases would make it convincing.
outcomes: Convert logits to probabilities with softmax and explain how logit gaps become probability ratios.
Compute cross-entropy from the probability given to the true token, and explain why logs are used.
Estimate the standard error of a measured pass rate and decide whether a difference is meaningful.
question: If two models differ by two percentage points on a 50-case test, how many cases would you need before you trusted that difference?
